clue.text: Person who is holy, competent and unwavering

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST as in place names like St Paul's
competent means able

explanation.surface: A description of a saintly, capable and steadfast person.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of three virtues, but only the last is the definition; the first two build the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and firm, never wobbling.

clue.text: County boy collecting duck — something coming on to computer

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the boy word takes in the duck, so its letters hold the zero inside them

parts.note: a boy is a lad
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A lad from a county picks up a duck while something arrives on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' puts O inside LAD to give LOAD. A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A file transferred from the internet onto your machine is a fetched item, something coming onto the computer.

clue.text: Very detailed autobiography of John the composer?

definitions.meaning: describing events step by step, missing nothing
John Blow was a 17th-century English composer, so his life story told by himself would be a book about Blow, written by Blow

explanation.surface: A thorough account of a composer's life written by the man himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A step-by-step account covering every moment is exhaustive; the whimsical second reading makes it the title of John Blow's memoir.

clue.text: Red gown or shift for malefactor

indicators.note: to shift letters is to move them about into a new order

explanation.surface: A scarlet robe or a loose dress, worn by a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a garment alongside the gown, but it is the anagram signal working on REDGOWNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is an evil-doer, someone who commits offences.

clue.text: Fixes up a bargain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to fix something in place is to pin it

explanation.surface: Someone renovates property they bought cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PINS to give the four letters, read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is British slang for something cheap, a real steal.

clue.text: Ongoing soap opera — corny stuff from what we hear?

indicators.note: signals that the word for corny stuff is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: corn and similar grains are cereal

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a long-running soap as corny rubbish they have heard about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corny' suggests trite, but it means made of corn: grain, or cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama broadcast in instalments that continue over time is a serial.

clue.text: Old-fashioned ad due to change — about time!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for time
the letters of ad due to change their places to form a new word

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that an old-fashioned advert is finally to be updated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' looks like part of the sentence, but 'to' is fodder: 'change' rearranges ADDUETO to OUTDAED, and 'about' puts T round inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer current or in fashion is out of date.

clue.text: Loose woman rendering song by old piano

parts.note: to troll is to sing in a full, carefree way, so to render a song
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals sings beside an old piano.
explanation.walkthrough: TROLL is an old verb for singing heartily, not the internet sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A trollop is a dated insult for a promiscuous or slovenly woman.

clue.text: Quiet time? One may get stuck into a book

definitions.text: One may get stuck into a book

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A quiet moment for someone engrossed in reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck into a book' sounds like an absorbed reader, but it means bound into one, as a leaf is.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is bound into the spine of a book, so it is literally stuck in.

clue.text: Musical composition given arrangement by our dean

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh, like a piece of music given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of music arranged by the cathedral dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' fits the musical surface but is the anagram signal on OURDEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a musical or poetic form with a recurring refrain, related to the rondo.

clue.text: Popular trend good for Paris — and with witty person joining in

indicators.note: the pieces join the French word by going inside it

parts.note: bon is the French for good, as spoken in Paris
taken as written
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A Paris fashion that a witty person happily joins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the city or a fashion capital, but 'good for Paris' just asks for the French word; 'joining in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump on the bandwagon is to follow a fashionable movement, so the word stands for a popular craze.

clue.text: One little fellow following pair was nosy

indicators.note: the one and little fellow come after the pair in the answer

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
Ed, a short form of Edward, is a little fellow's name

explanation.surface: A small man trailing a couple was snooping on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little fellow' means a short name, ED, not a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying means poking into matters that are none of your business, being inquisitive.

clue.text: English lad comes across knight in the wood

indicators.note: the lad's letters go across, round the knight, enclosing him

parts.note: a lad is a boy
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An English boy meets a knight in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wood' looks like a forest setting for the meeting, but it is the definition: a kind of timber. 'comes across' puts N inside BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard dark timber from tropical trees.

clue.text: Old garment is what you see in the middle of battle!

parts.words: is what you see in the middle of battle!
parts.note: the two central letters of the word battle are a pair of the same letter, a twin of the twentieth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An old garment is what a soldier sees in the heat of combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of the word 'battle' is TT, a T twice over; say that as a phrase and you have the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was a close-fitting jacket worn by men from the 14th to 17th centuries.

clue.text: Spontaneous, like one given no help on stage?

definitions.meaning: done of one's own accord, without being asked

definitions.text: like one given no help on stage?
definitions.meaning: an actor who forgets a line and gets no whispered cue from the wings has received no reminder

explanation.surface: An actor improvises freely when nobody feeds them a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without a cue or urging is spontaneous; whimsically it is an actor with no prompter's help.

clue.text: Bob? If properly organised could be this early

indicators.note: the letters are put in proper order, rearranged into the word they could become

explanation.surface: A remark that a bob haircut, if well done, could be ready this early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name, but it is a haircut, and the question mark flags it as one example. 'properly organised' rearranges THISEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, one example of a way of dressing the head.

clue.text: Dad is 'ample', greed possibly producing this?

definitions.text: Dad is 'ample', greed possibly producing this?

indicators.note: these letters could possibly be another arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad claims he is merely ample, but his greed has clearly given him a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges DADISAMPLEGREED. The whole clue is also the definition: a greedy dad in later years who calls himself 'ample' has the bulge in question.
explanation.definitionFit: The thickening of the waist many people gain in their forties and fifties is the paunch named here.

clue.text: Friend and fellow competitor not v. Significant

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: the competitor word must do without the abbreviation for versus

parts.note: a rival competes against you
v. is the abbreviation for versus, as in a fixture list

explanation.surface: A friend and fellow competitor are not playing against each other, which is unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not v.' sounds like 'not versus', but it means remove the letter V from RIVAL, leaving RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A material point is one that is relevant and important.

clue.text: Making electrically safe object that's attached to organ

indicators.note: the object word is joined on after the organ word

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Describing a device clipped to the ear that has been made electrically safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a musical instrument or a body part like the heart; it is the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecting an appliance to the ground so faults discharge harmlessly is the British term for grounding a circuit.

clue.text: One responsible for the cast

parts.note: reads like a theatre director choosing actors, but cast means a throw, as of dice or a fishing line

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of picking the actors for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a casting director; instead it is whoever made the throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to throw, so the person who made the cast is the one who hurled it.

clue.text: See anger mounting in the road

indicators.note: the reversed word sits within the road abbreviation
in a down clue, mounting means going upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: anger is rage

explanation.surface: Watch rage building up on the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a verb here, to look at, not a noun for a bishop's seat. 'mounting' signals the turn upwards, which in a down entry means backwards, and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it, to view it.

clue.text: Monsters getting in the way of progress

indicators.note: the letters are found in the word progress, hidden within it

explanation.surface: Monstrous obstacles block the path of advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in the way of' reads as obstructing, but it shows the answer sitting inside the word 'progress'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, the classic fairy-tale monster.

clue.text: Provision with flexibility built in?

definitions.meaning: a stock or store kept for use
the adverb from supple, meaning done in a bendy, flexible way

explanation.surface: Stores that include some leeway for change.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision is a stock of goods; whimsically, an adverb meaning in a pliant fashion.

clue.text: Twenty losing head and heart

indicators.note: the word for twenty loses its first letter

parts.note: a score is twenty

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head and their heart at twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORE without its first letter, S, leaves the four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The core is the central or innermost part, the heart of something.

clue.text: Like a monarch — sincere, good within

indicators.note: the letter for good sits inside the sincere word

parts.note: sincere means real, genuine

explanation.surface: A monarch who is honest, with goodness inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts G inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, befitting a king or queen.

clue.text: Remain fresh as a model

definitions.meaning: food that keeps without going off endures
a cobbler's foot-shaped form on which shoes are made

explanation.surface: Something that stays as fresh as a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or keep is one sense; the other is the wooden foot-shaped form a shoemaker builds on.

clue.text: Sort of vessel one found in posh port being renovated

indicators.note: the numeral for one is placed within the rearranged letters
renovated means remade, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A ship discovered in a smart harbour undergoing refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being renovated' rearranges POSHPORT, and 'found in' places I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A troopship is a vessel for transporting soldiers.

clue.text: A divine figure, endlessly old, appearing in the mist

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: the word old loses its last letter, having no end

explanation.surface: A god of love, ancient as ever, emerges through the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the D from OLD to give OL.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a fine spray of liquid droplets, a mist.

clue.text: Bird diving into each lake and never stopping

indicators.note: the bird goes inside the abbreviation for each, like a seabird plunging into water

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird endlessly plunges into every lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is the obvious definition candidate, but the definition is 'never stopping' at the end; 'diving into' is the insertion signal, apt for a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, without end.
